# software-engineering

> Tag: software-engineering

## Posts

- [just run make](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/11/13/just-run-make.md): The task runners just and run win converts by removing Make's restrictions. Those restrictions are Chesterton's fences: they skip unchanged work, parallelize for free, give every caller the same commands, and keep an untested application out of your build.
- [Why Can't I Just Write schema.sql?](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/11/07/why-not-just-schema-sql.md): Shrinking Stockroom's DuckDB warehouses by 99% meant confronting why declarative schemas, numbered SQL migrations, and in-place SQL all fall short on their own.
- [The Software-Engineering Amish](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/10/28/software-engineering-amish.md): In October 2026 r/opensource banned AI by decree and walked it back in days, while Codeberg banned it by member vote. The positions forming around AI-written code map onto 1812 closely enough to predict from, if I write the prediction down and date it.
- [The Suite Life of Bobs and Code](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/05/10/slobac.md): SLOBAC delivers principles for good tests, a taxonomy of test smells, safe refactoring workflows, and an agent skill to audit and clean up sprawling AI-generated test suites.
- [The Load-Bearing Pipeline Was Human](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/03/21/the-load-bearing-pipeline-was-human.md): A specification-to-code pipeline that worked for decades doesn't stop working because you swapped the executors; it stops working when you rip out the stages.
- [Moving Fast, Breaking Nothing](https://blog.cani.ne.jp/2026/03/13/seven-weeks.md): A diary of building a16n - from empty repo to shipping CLI in 46 days, nine phases, and a mid-project architectural redesign. Every milestone finished early. Nothing broke.
